doe-osti-3363938-deflagration-to-detonat:
Sandia National Laboratories report SAND2026-20840, by Michael L. Hobbs and printed in May 2026, updates XDDT, a code that models how a burning explosive transitions into a detonation. The update converts the code from centimeter-gram-second units to SI units. It adds adaptive gridding that refines the mesh where the action is. It also couples in the TIGER equation of state library for product gases.

Unit conversion exposed real bugs, and the report documents each correction: two namelist variables were dimensionally reclassified, and the Mie-Grüneisen solid thermal pressure treatment was fixed. Comparisons show the JWL equation of state underpredicts pressure at moderate expansion and temperatures above about 2000 kelvin, where the TIGER treatment does better. The report links the pre-ignition chemistry code XCHEM to XDDT through a solution handoff, completing the path from thermal ignition to detonation.
doe-osti-3365157-highlight-of-ic-project: A Los Alamos highlight slide, LA-UR-26-24281, by Xiangrong Fu (May 2026), showcases Institutional Computing project w25_dreamxd. The DREAMxD code models Earth's radiation belts, donut-shaped zones where million-electron-volt electrons circle trapped by the magnetic field. The project's advance is speed. A new algorithm computes the quasilinear diffusion coefficients the code needs. For a large problem it runs about 100 times faster than the standard approach, measured in node hours. The hosted text is a single slide with one figure and one reference.
